VACUUM every production table
Only display the databricks.yml filename
explanation: bundle validate checks the configuration for the selected target. It is a useful gate before deployment, alongside appropriate application tests.

prompt: A production bundle should follow production deployment constraints. Which target setting expresses that intent?
options: mode: production
mode: notebook-local
mode: unrestricted
mode: checkpoint
explanation: Production mode applies deployment behavior and validation intended for production. It is separate from the target name and environment-specific resource overrides.
code:
targets:
  prod:
    mode: production
    workspace:
      host: https://production-workspace.example

prompt: What best supports promoting reviewed changes from development to production?
options: Copy whatever notebook happens to be open on the developer laptop
Deploy only notebook outputs without their source
Edit production resources manually after every pull request
Version code and resource definitions, run checks, then deploy the intended revision to the target
explanation: A reproducible CI/CD path ties tested source and definitions to a specific revision and target. Ad hoc copies weaken traceability.

prompt: An unattended deployment pipeline needs Databricks access. What identity pattern is appropriate?
options: A shared browser session cookie committed to Git
An unauthenticated Jobs API call
A scoped service principal using supported OAuth machine-to-machine authentication
A developer password pasted into databricks.yml
explanation: Service principals and machine-to-machine authentication provide an automation identity. Credentials should be supplied through protected CI mechanisms rather than committed files.

prompt: A team uses Databricks Git folders for development. What should remain the source of truth for repeatable deployment?
options: Only the text of the last successful job notification
The reviewed source revision and versioned resource configuration
Each developer current uncommitted workspace edits
Only the installed runtime package cache
explanation: Git folders support source workflows. Reproducible deployment requires a known source revision and versioned definitions, with environment changes controlled through configuration.

prompt: A lakehouse must preserve raw input for replay, cleanse entities, and serve analytical aggregates. Which layer assignment fits?
options: Bronze for raw input, silver for validated/refined data, gold for business-ready models
Bronze for all business aggregates, gold for original raw payloads
Silver only for credentials and bronze only for dashboards
Use all three names for identical copies without distinct responsibilities
explanation: The medallion pattern separates raw ingestion, validated/refined data, and business-ready analytics. This supports replay and progressive quality.

prompt: A sales fact table is defined at one row per order line. Why must dimension joins respect that grain?
options: Every dimension must contain exactly one row total
Fact grain changes automatically to match any joined table
Dimensions must be stored only as driver variables
Nonunique dimension matches can multiply fact rows and distort measures
explanation: Dimensional modeling requires a clear fact grain and compatible relationships. Multiple matches can duplicate measures unless the query intentionally handles that cardinality.

prompt: An analytical model must show a customer category as it was when an order occurred. Which modeling approach supports this?
options: Replace every historical category with NULL
Join all customer versions on customer ID without temporal criteria
SCD Type 2 dimension versions joined using the order time and validity interval
Only the latest SCD Type 1 category for every past order
explanation: Type 2 history preserves attribute validity intervals. An as-of join selects the version applicable to the fact event and avoids multiplying rows across all versions.

prompt: A large fact table has evolving filters on customer and date, and many small files. What design combines layout adaptability and balanced files?
options: Storing one tiny file per fact row
Appropriate liquid clustering keys with compaction maintenance
Partitioning on every unique transaction ID and never compacting
Combining ZORDER and liquid clustering on the same table
explanation: Liquid clustering supports evolving access patterns, while compaction improves file sizes. High-cardinality directory partitions can fragment the data layout.

prompt: Many dashboards reuse the same expensive daily sales aggregation. Which object can store and refresh that result?
options: A materialized view
A temporary view that recomputes the full query on every read
A row filter on the raw sales table
A notebook variable containing the last driver collect result
explanation: A materialized view persists precomputed query results and refreshes them. It can reduce repeated aggregate computation for downstream consumers.

prompt: Different dashboards disagree on the definition of net revenue. Which feature centralizes a reusable governed metric definition?
options: Separate copied SQL expressions in each dashboard
A file-level clustering key called revenue
A job retry policy
A Unity Catalog metric view
explanation: Metric views define reusable measures and dimensions centrally. Consumers can query the same metric definition instead of maintaining divergent dashboard calculations.

prompt: In a metric view, what is the difference between a dimension and a measure?
options: Dimensions define user passwords and measures define table owners
Both must store one fixed total that never changes with grouping
A dimension supplies grouping/filtering fields; a measure supplies an aggregation expression evaluated at the requested grain
A dimension always contains a SUM and a measure is always a raw text field
explanation: Metric views separate fields used to group/filter from measure definitions. Measures can be evaluated at the grouping level requested by the query.

prompt: Why define a ratio such as revenue per order using aggregate measures rather than averaging arbitrary row-level ratios?
options: Grouping never affects any ratio
The ratio must be evaluated at the requested aggregation grain to preserve its intended meaning
Every row-level ratio has the same denominator automatically
Metric views prohibit all division
explanation: A ratio of aggregates and an average of per-row ratios can differ. Measure expressions should encode the intended calculation at the query grain.

prompt: Two streams join machine readings to maintenance events by machine ID. State grows despite watermarks. Matches should occur within 20 minutes. What additional join condition is needed?
options: An event-time range linking the two timestamps within the allowed matching interval
A sort of the output by machine ID after the join
A larger checkpoint retention period without changing the predicate
A GROUP BY machine ID before every write with no time restriction
explanation: Watermarks describe lateness, while an event-time constraint lets the engine determine when old join rows can no longer match future input. An equality key alone does not bound matching time.

prompt: A left outer stream-stream join has not yet emitted a NULL match for a recent sensor event. Why can this be correct?
options: Outer stream joins always drop unmatched left rows permanently
A left outer join emits a NULL row before checking any right-side events
Unmatched rows are released only after deleting the checkpoint
The engine must wait until the relevant watermark and time bound rule out a future matching event
explanation: A streaming outer join cannot immediately declare that no future match will arrive. Watermarks and the matching-time bound establish when an unmatched result can be finalized.

prompt: A stream enriches new events from a slowly changing Delta lookup table. A lookup value is corrected. What happens to old output rows and the next micro-batch?
options: The lookup remains frozen at the first micro-batch for the lifetime of the query
The join becomes stateful and requires a watermark on the lookup table
New input uses the latest valid lookup version; old enriched output is not automatically rewritten
The correction retroactively updates every previously written output row
explanation: A Delta stream-static join enriches each micro-batch with the latest valid static table version. Updating the lookup does not itself replay already emitted streaming output.

prompt: One input stream advances much more slowly than the other. Why can the default global watermark retain state for longer?
options: The global watermark is the average of both wall-clock processing times
The default min policy advances at the slowest input watermark to protect slower data
The default policy uses the fastest input watermark and drops all slower data
The checkpoint fixes the watermark permanently at query start
explanation: The default multiple-watermark policy uses the minimum input watermark. A max policy advances faster but can discard data from slower inputs; it is a correctness tradeoff.

prompt: A windowed aggregation uses complete output mode because every trigger must return the full result table. What state behavior should be expected?
options: The full aggregate state is retained rather than evicting old windows simply because the watermark advanced
Every emitted window is immediately removed from state
Complete mode automatically deduplicates all business event IDs
Complete mode writes only newly finalized rows
explanation: Complete mode preserves the result table needed to emit all aggregate rows. Its state behavior differs from watermark-based final-window append output.

prompt: A failed foreachBatch Delta append is retried with the same batch. Which writer options can identify and ignore the duplicate transaction?
options: A new random txnAppId on every retry and a fixed txnVersion of zero
A fresh checkpoint on every retry with ordinary append writes
A different output table name for each retry
A stable txnAppId and the same txnVersion for that batch
explanation: Delta can recognize a repeated write using the application ID and transaction version. Both identifiers must identify the same logical batch on its retry.

prompt: A query using batch IDs as txnVersion restarts from a deliberately fresh checkpoint. Why must its txnAppId generation change?
options: A fresh checkpoint makes Delta append writes nontransactional
Changing only the query display name automatically resets all transaction identifiers
Batch IDs restart at zero, so the old application ID could cause genuinely new writes to be treated as already committed
The table no longer accepts any integer transaction versions
explanation: A fresh checkpoint restarts batch numbering. A new application ID distinguishes the new generation from transactions recorded under the previous checkpoint.

prompt: A foreachBatch callback commits to Delta table A, then fails before writing table B. Which recovery assumption is sound?
options: The callback cannot ever be invoked again once one sink committed
Each sink needs safe retry handling; the two separate writes are not one atomic cross-table transaction
Both tables automatically roll back because the callback failed
Table A always deletes its latest successful transaction during checkpoint recovery
explanation: Separate sink writes can leave a partially completed batch. Make each effect idempotent or provide a recovery strategy rather than assuming callback-wide atomicity.

prompt: An AUTO CDC Type 2 target must answer which customer attributes applied at an earlier sequence value. Which generated metadata supports that history?
options: __START_AT and __END_AT boundaries for each stored version
Only the latest ingestion filename
Only a count of rows per customer
Only the current value with no version boundaries
explanation: Type 2 history stores versions with sequence-based validity boundaries. Those boundaries allow selecting the version applicable to an earlier point.

prompt: A scheduled serverless job has a generous completion window and can tolerate slower startup. Which mode should be evaluated for lower cost?
options: Performance-optimized mode solely because it is the default
A notebook-only standard mode setting applied to all interactive users
An init script that disables serverless provisioning
Standard mode for the job, subject to meeting its completion requirement
explanation: Standard mode trades startup latency for potential cost savings on supported jobs and pipelines. Measure whether the workload still meets its required completion window.

prompt: A short serverless job is triggered by an interactive workflow and needs minimal startup delay. Which supported mode best matches that priority?
options: A cluster-scoped init script selecting local mode
An unsupported Spark configuration that reserves executors forever
Performance-optimized mode
Standard mode regardless of its slower startup
explanation: Performance-optimized mode keeps warm capacity for faster starts. Standard mode is intended for workloads that can tolerate a longer startup delay.

prompt: A pure transformation has no sorting contract. Its unit test fails only because identical rows appear in a different order. What should the test do?
options: Change production logic to collect all rows to the driver
Compare the complete row content without requiring an unspecified row order
Compare only row counts and omit all value assertions
Sort only the expected rows but leave actual rows unordered
explanation: Spark DataFrame row order is not an implicit contract. Equality checks should validate all values while requiring ordering only when the transformation promises it.

prompt: A For each job processes 40 source tables. Running all nested tasks together overloads the source system. Which setting directly limits concurrent iterations?
options: The For each task concurrency setting
The number of columns selected by each SQL query
The catalog BROWSE privilege
The job task-value JSON key name
explanation: For each concurrency limits simultaneous executions of the nested task. Choose it according to source capacity and workload requirements instead of launching every iteration together.

prompt: In a CDC source contract, a NULL attribute means that field was not supplied, rather than an instruction to erase it. Which AUTO CDC behavior fits?
options: Always overwrite every target attribute with NULL
Remove the business key and append each change as a new entity
Use Type 2 alone and assume it changes NULL semantics
Enable ignore_null_updates so existing attribute values survive omitted NULL updates
explanation: ignore_null_updates preserves existing values for NULL update fields under that source contract. Use this only when NULL means no change, because intentional clearing requires different handling.

prompt: A downstream customer replica must apply source updates and deletes. The engineer enables skipChangeCommits on a plain Delta stream. What is missing?
options: Only a higher number of shuffle partitions
Only sorting source rows by customer ID
Read Change Data Feed and apply its change operations, or use another design that propagates mutations
Only a larger maxFilesPerTrigger value
explanation: skipChangeCommits avoids processing modifying commits; it does not replicate those updates and deletes. CDF exposes operation records that a downstream consumer can apply.

prompt: CSV files have no header row, but Auto Loader treats the first row as column names. What should be configured?
options: A larger output-file size
header=false together with a suitable schema or schema strategy
A shorter event-time watermark
A SELECT grant on each inferred column
explanation: Auto Loader assumes CSV headers unless configured otherwise. The reader contract must match the actual file structure to avoid losing or misinterpreting the first record.

prompt: A schema hint asks the Parquet reader to read a column as a chosen type, but a file contains an incompatible value. What should the engineer understand?
options: A schema hint is not an unconditional cast; mismatched content can be rescued
The hint guarantees every value is converted successfully
The hint automatically deletes incompatible files from storage
The hint disables the streaming checkpoint
explanation: Schema hints guide the reader. They do not guarantee arbitrary conversions; rescued data preserves incompatible content for investigation.

prompt: Each source file contains one pretty-printed JSON document across several lines. A line-oriented reader treats the lines as malformed records. Which option fits the file contract?
options: maxFilesPerTrigger=1 without changing JSON parsing
A complete streaming output mode
A null-safe join condition on the filename
multiLine=true for the JSON reader
explanation: The multiLine JSON option supports a JSON document spanning multiple lines. Rate limiting and output modes do not change the reader record boundary.

prompt: A supported MySQL Lakeflow Connect pipeline must capture row changes. Which source configuration matches the documented setup?
options: Only an hourly full-table CSV export
Only a target Delta table with no source setup
Binary logging enabled with ROW format, FULL row images, and replication privileges
Statement-only logging with no replication user
explanation: The MySQL connector uses binlog replication. Its documented source setup requires row-based full images and the appropriate privileges and connectivity; availability is Public Preview.

prompt: A SQL Server source table has a primary key and supports both change tracking and CDC. What does the connector documentation recommend for optimal performance?
options: Use Auto Loader directly against SQL Server transaction logs
Change tracking; when both are enabled, the connector uses change tracking
CDC is always used even when change tracking is enabled
Disable both and rely on a full table scan for every change
explanation: The connector recommends change tracking for tables with primary keys and CDC when no primary key is available. If both mechanisms are enabled, change tracking is used.

prompt: A supported Structured Streaming workload reads an Amazon Kinesis message stream directly. Which source format identifies that connector?
options: kinesis
cloudFiles
jdbc
delta
explanation: The Kinesis connector uses the kinesis streaming format with stream and access configuration. Auto Loader is for cloud files, not a direct Kinesis message-stream reader.

prompt: A supported Google Cloud workload reads Pub/Sub directly using the Spark connector. Which configuration identifies the message source?
options: format("cloudFiles") with the topic name as a file extension
format("jdbc") with a Pub/Sub topic as the SQL database
format("delta") with no subscription or source connection
format("pubsub") with projectId, topicId, subscriptionId, and supported authentication
explanation: The Pub/Sub reader uses its own source format and source identifiers. Use the documented authentication and runtime support for the selected environment.

prompt: Analysts must keep querying a retained lakehouse copy while an operational database is temporarily unavailable. Which acquisition design better supports that requirement?
options: Create a foreign catalog without a working connection
Replace remote credentials with a source-schema comment
Ingest and retain a governed replica, with an explicit freshness policy during source outages
Use only live federation and assume it can query an unavailable remote system
explanation: Federation queries the external system in place. A retained ingested copy supports local reads during a source outage, although its freshness is limited until ingestion resumes.

prompt: Two partners need approved analyses of combined sensitive data but do not want to grant each other unrestricted raw-table reads. Which approach fits?
options: A public storage path containing both complete datasets
A Clean Room collaboration with approved workloads and controlled outputs
An unrestricted open share containing every raw column
A shared source-database administrator credential
explanation: Clean Rooms provides a controlled computation collaboration model. Sharing raw assets and credentials does not provide the same restriction on what each partner can inspect.

prompt: The latest customer timestamp is shared by two records. RANK followed by rank=1 keeps both. How can a batch transformation choose one deterministically?
options: ROW_NUMBER ordered by timestamp and a stable unique tie-breaker, then keep row 1
RANK ordered only by the same timestamp again
DISTINCT on all columns without selecting a version
COUNT(*) over the customer and keep every counted row
explanation: RANK preserves ties. ROW_NUMBER can select a single record, but its ordering needs a stable tie-breaker to make that selection deterministic.

prompt: After a customer LEFT JOIN orders, a customer with no matching orders has one output row with NULL order_id. Which aggregate counts that customer as having zero orders?
options: COUNT(*)
COUNT(c.customer_id)
COUNT(COALESCE(o.order_id, c.customer_id))
COUNT(o.order_id)
explanation: COUNT of the nullable right-side key counts only matched non-NULL values. COUNT(*) counts the NULL-extended join row, which would report one instead of zero.

prompt: A VARIANT object contains an explicit JSON null at field archived_at. Which test identifies that encoded null?
options: COUNT(*) on the containing table
CAST(document AS BINARY) IS NULL
is_variant_null(document:archived_at)
document:archived_at IS NULL as an equivalent test in every case
explanation: A VARIANT-encoded JSON null differs from SQL NULL. is_variant_null tests the encoded null, while IS NULL tests the SQL-null value.

prompt: Two source rows match the same target key and both qualify for an update. What should a MERGE pipeline do before applying them?
options: Use INSERT-only logic and assume source duplicates disappear
Resolve the source to one intended update per target key using the source ordering contract
Assume MERGE always picks the first physical source row
Remove the ON condition so both rows can update every target row
explanation: An update with multiple qualifying source matches can be ambiguous. Preprocess the source according to the business ordering contract rather than relying on physical row order.

prompt: A quality rule quantity > 0 routes TRUE rows to clean and FALSE rows to quarantine. NULL quantities reach neither branch. How should routing be completed?
options: Explicitly classify NULL quantities as invalid and route them with their original payload
Keep only the two predicates and assume NOT NULL evaluates to TRUE
Replace every missing quantity with a valid positive value
Remove the quality flag before calculating counts
explanation: SQL predicates with NULL evaluate to unknown, so neither TRUE nor FALSE filtering captures them. Explicit invalid-NULL handling preserves the reconciliation between input and outputs.

prompt: An enrichment query uses ai_query with failOnError=false. What must happen before its responses become trusted downstream classification labels?
options: Treat every returned row as a valid prediction because the SQL query completed
Remove all rows with uncommon text before checking inference outcomes
Change the endpoint name to the output table name
Inspect per-row error information and validate successful responses against the expected output contract
explanation: A non-failing query can contain row-level inference failures or unusable results. Validate the response and error fields before publishing classifications.

prompt: A rule requires the daily source and target row totals to reconcile. Why should it be implemented as aggregate validation rather than an aggregate function inside a row expectation?
options: Every aggregate inside an expectation is converted into a watermark
A table comment is sufficient to enforce the totals
Row expectations evaluate record constraints; cross-row totals need separately computed validation results
Row expectations automatically aggregate every upstream table
explanation: Compute aggregate validation values in an appropriate dataset or task, then evaluate them. Per-record expectation expressions do not themselves define cross-row reconciliation.

objective: Apply CDF operations to current state
prompt: A latest-state replica consumes a CDF update containing both update_preimage and update_postimage. Which record should supply the new row value?
options: Ignore all updates and process only insert records
Apply the update_postimage to the current row; do not treat the preimage as a second new state
Append both images as two current rows
Delete every row whenever an update_preimage appears
explanation: The preimage describes the old value and the postimage the new one. A current-state replica applies the new image and handles delete events separately.

prompt: A Delta streaming source reports increasing numFilesOutstanding while the query remains active. What does that metric indicate?
options: The number of source files waiting to be processed is growing
The number of target files removed by VACUUM is growing
The number of invalid SQL alert definitions is growing
The number of rows currently stored in every state operator is growing
explanation: Source backlog metrics describe unprocessed input. They help distinguish ingestion lag from target-file maintenance or state-store size.

prompt: A stateful query reports a rising numRowsDroppedByWatermark value. Which investigation is most directly relevant?
options: Increase table-comment length to preserve more metadata
Treat every dropped row as a duplicate regardless of its timestamp
Reset the checkpoint without assessing replay and sink effects
Compare observed event lateness with the configured watermark and business acceptance requirements
explanation: The metric indicates rows rejected as too late for the stateful operation. Review timestamp quality, delays, and allowed lateness before changing the policy.

prompt: Input volume is stable, but stateOperators memoryUsedBytes and numRowsTotal keep growing over hours. What should be examined?
options: Only the names of job notification recipients
Only the target schema comments
The stateful operators, matching-time bounds, and watermark progress
Only the size of the current notebook output cell
explanation: State growth can reveal missing or ineffective cleanup boundaries. Inspect the stateful plan and event-time progress rather than assuming that stable input rate means bounded state.

prompt: Several streaming writes run on classic compute. What makes their progress views easier to distinguish in the Spark UI?
options: Disable all progress events
Assign a unique queryName to each streaming write
Use the same checkpoint directory for all writes
Give all streams the same unnamed temporary view
explanation: A query name labels streaming query progress for identification. It does not replace the unique checkpoint each query needs.

prompt: A serverless workload needs query-performance diagnosis, but the engineer expects a classic-compute Spark UI. Which available tool should be used?
options: The query profile and query history for serverless execution details
A cluster-local Spark UI assumed to exist for every serverless task
Only a source file count with no execution details
Only the bundle resource display name
explanation: The serverless documentation directs query-performance diagnosis to the query profile rather than the unavailable classic Spark UI.

prompt: A streaming query is processing one long micro-batch. Neither onQueryProgress nor onQueryIdle has appeared recently. What is the correct initial interpretation?
options: The checkpoint must always be deleted immediately
All source records must have been permanently lost
The query must have finished successfully
Silence alone does not prove failure; inspect the active batch and query status
explanation: Progress events occur at batch completion and idle events when waiting for data. A long active batch can be healthy while neither event is emitted.

prompt: A compaction experiment reduces file count, but a selective query still reads nearly the same bytes. What evidence is needed before claiming improved pruning?
options: Assume fewer files always means proportionally fewer matching rows
Infer a faster join solely from the number of table columns
Compare scan/pruning metrics for the same predicate and data under comparable conditions
Use only the new table name as the success measure
explanation: Compaction reduces file overhead, while pruning depends on statistics and layout relative to the predicate. Measure actual scan work rather than equating file count with skipping.

prompt: A cold baseline query is compared with a warm cached run after OPTIMIZE. The second is faster. What can be concluded?
options: The cache must be disabled permanently for every production workload
The experiment confounds caching and layout effects, so it does not isolate the benefit of OPTIMIZE
The full improvement proves the clustering keys are optimal
OPTIMIZE guarantees every future query will have the same latency
explanation: Caching can materially change repeated-read performance. Compare controlled conditions to attribute improvements to a specific layout change.

prompt: On a supported liquid-clustered Delta table, keys are changed to match new query patterns. Which operation can fully recluster existing data using the current keys?
options: OPTIMIZE the table with FULL
VACUUM the table before any rewrite
GRANT SELECT on the new key columns
Change only the table comment
explanation: Changing clustering metadata does not fully reorganize historical files. OPTIMIZE FULL performs a full reclustering on supported configurations.

prompt: A team assumes predictive optimization will maintain its explicit ZORDER layout automatically. What should it verify?
options: Every predictive OPTIMIZE command automatically repeats the previous ZORDER columns
Predictive optimization converts every table to directory partitioning
Predictive optimization has no table maintenance capabilities
Predictive optimization does not perform ZORDER; consider supported automatic liquid clustering or explicit ZORDER maintenance as appropriate
explanation: Predictive optimization automates supported maintenance but does not execute ZORDER. Automatic liquid clustering uses a different layout and requires its supported configuration.

prompt: A batch CDF consumer durably applied all changes through version 207. Versions 208–210 exist and remain retained. What starting version avoids replaying version 207?
options: 210 only
The table creation version regardless of progress
explanation: Batch CDF version ranges include their starting version. Starting at the next unprocessed retained version prevents unnecessarily replaying the last fully applied version.

prompt: A downstream audit process needs a year of row-change history, while the source retains only a short CDF window. Which design supports durable long-term analysis?
options: Reduce source history retention to zero to simplify the audit
Continuously archive available CDF events into a separately governed retained table
Assume source CDF keeps every change forever
Query only the latest source rows to reconstruct all deleted values
explanation: Source CDF follows transient retained history. Archive changes before they expire when long-term history is required, with suitable retention and governance on the archive.

prompt: A table contains duplicate business records. Its small files are compacted with OPTIMIZE. What logical result should be expected?
options: Duplicate rows remain unless a separate deduplication transformation removes them
OPTIMIZE automatically keeps only the newest row per business key
Compaction converts duplicate rows into primary-key violations
Compaction changes every duplicate into a deletion-vector tombstone
explanation: OPTIMIZE changes physical layout while preserving logical row content. Deduplication is a separate data transformation requiring a business key and selection rule.

objective: Treat managed and external maintenance differently
prompt: A Unity Catalog external table is not receiving the predictive maintenance expected for a managed table. What should the owner understand?
options: Every external table automatically has identical predictive maintenance to a managed table
The missing maintenance means SELECT privileges can never be granted
Renaming the table makes its external storage managed without migration
Predictive optimization is for supported Unity Catalog managed tables; external-table maintenance must be planned separately
explanation: Table ownership and storage-management type affect available automation. Verify supported managed-table features and retain responsibility for external data maintenance.

prompt: Invalid rows containing raw personal identifiers are sent to quarantine. The clean target is masked. What protection is still required?
options: Assume masking the clean target physically rewrites all quarantine values
Grant every dashboard user ownership of quarantine for debugging
Restrict and govern quarantine access because raw sensitive data can remain there
Treat quarantine as public because its rows failed validation
explanation: Quality failure does not remove sensitivity. Apply appropriate access, masking, and retention controls to raw and quarantine data as well as published outputs.

prompt: A column mask returns the original value for an authorized account group and a replacement for others. What determines the value visible during a user query?
options: Only the table storage path name
The policy function evaluated for the querying user identity
Only the identity that originally inserted the row
Only the alphabetical order of group names
explanation: Query-time column-mask logic uses the relevant user identity and policy conditions. The writer identity alone does not define what each later reader sees.
code:
RETURN CASE WHEN is_account_group_member('sensitive_readers')
  THEN value ELSE '[hidden]' END;

prompt: A pipeline must build a secured output from complete source values, but its run-as identity is masked on the source. What must be addressed?
options: Authorize the required source access for the pipeline identity and govern the output for its readers
Grant SELECT alone and assume it always bypasses every mask
Disable quality expectations and assume masks stop applying
Change only the pipeline display name
explanation: A refresh can persist values visible to its run identity, including masked values. Deliberately authorize the processing identity where required, while preserving appropriate controls on the resulting output.

prompt: An organization exposes a masked customer view to analysts. Why should it avoid also granting those analysts unrestricted reads of the unmasked base table?
options: The view automatically revokes every base-table grant when queried
Masked views physically erase all original base values
SELECT on the base table affects only table comments
The extra base-table access can expose values the view was meant to protect
explanation: A curated access layer does not make an independently granted raw-data path safe. Least-privilege grants must align with the intended protection boundary.

prompt: A user has MANAGE on a table and the required usage privileges, but no SELECT grant. What does MANAGE itself provide?
options: Only permission to add a notebook comment
An automatic transfer of table ownership to the user
Object/privilege management, not automatic data-read privileges; specific access must be granted separately
Automatic unrestricted SELECT on every table in the metastore
explanation: MANAGE is not automatic possession of every data privilege. Holders can manage permissions and can explicitly grant themselves supported privileges, so grant it deliberately.

prompt: A governed tag is set on a catalog. Will every child column automatically carry that tag for a column-matching ABAC rule?
options: No; governed tags cannot be used by any ABAC policy
No; ABAC can implicitly inherit tags through object levels, but tags do not inherit to columns
Yes; every column always receives a materialized copy of every catalog tag
Yes; table usage grants automatically copy all tags onto every column
explanation: ABAC has implicit tag inheritance for object levels, but not columns. A rule matching tagged columns requires the appropriate column classification rather than assuming catalog tags propagate to them.

prompt: A service principal must create tables in one existing schema and has no prior access. Which scoped privileges form the necessary access path?
options: USE CATALOG on the catalog, USE SCHEMA and CREATE TABLE on the intended schema
SELECT only on the schema comment
CREATE TABLE on an unrelated catalog with no usage privileges
Ownership of every catalog in the metastore
explanation: CREATE TABLE does not eliminate the parent usage requirements. Scope the creation privilege to the intended schema with the necessary catalog/schema access.

prompt: Task A commits a valid Delta write, then downstream task B fails. What should be expected without custom compensation logic?
options: Every successful table write in the job automatically rolls back
The job drops the output catalog before reporting failure
The source checkpoint is automatically deleted
Task A remains committed; the job graph does not automatically roll back all successful task writes
explanation: Job orchestration is not a transaction spanning all task effects. Repair failed work or apply deliberate compensation rather than assuming a failed job undoes successful commits.

prompt: Bundle configuration validates, but the production run identity cannot read an input table. Which validation would expose that gap?
options: Only a unit test that compares literal integers
Only changing the deployment target label to prod
An integration test using the intended run identity and representative target environment
Only another filename check for databricks.yml
explanation: Bundle validation checks configuration, while an integration run verifies identity, dependencies and data access. Both serve distinct purposes.

prompt: A production bundle has been deployed, and the engineer now needs to execute its ingest_orders job resource. Which command fits?
options: databricks bundle init -t prod ingest_orders
databricks bundle run -t prod ingest_orders
databricks bundle validate -t prod ingest_orders
databricks workspace list ingest_orders
explanation: bundle run executes a resource referenced by its bundle key in the selected target. Validation and deployment do not themselves imply that the job has executed.

prompt: A task using the default success dependency condition is skipped because its upstream task failed. Where should diagnosis start?
options: Investigate the upstream failure and dependency outcome before treating the skipped task as a code failure
Immediately rewrite the skipped task because it necessarily threw an exception
Delete all successful task output without checking the failure
Assume the job scheduler ignored the dependency graph
explanation: A skipped task may never have executed its code. Run details and dependency conditions distinguish an upstream failure from a failure inside that task.

prompt: A Type 2 dimension uses validity intervals with an exclusive end timestamp. Which predicate selects the version active at a fact timestamp, including the current open-ended version?
options: fact_time >= valid_from without any end boundary
fact_time <= valid_to only, ignoring NULL and valid_from
Join every version on the business key without a time predicate
fact_time >= valid_from AND (valid_to IS NULL OR fact_time < valid_to)
explanation: For the stated half-open interval contract, the start is inclusive and the end exclusive. Explicit NULL handling includes the currently active dimension version and avoids adjacent-version double matches.

prompt: Two rows have revenue/units of 20/1 and 80/9. A measure defines revenue per unit as SUM(revenue)/SUM(units). What is its combined value?
options: Approximately 14.44
explanation: The defined measure divides the combined revenue of 100 by the combined units of 10. Averaging row-level ratios would produce a different metric.
code:
SELECT SUM(revenue) / SUM(units) AS revenue_per_unit
FROM VALUES (20, 1), (80, 9) AS sales(revenue, units);

prompt: A team needs consistent reusable business metric definitions and also wants an expensive summary precomputed. Which distinction is correct?
options: Neither object can participate in governed analytics
Metric views centralize measure semantics; materialized views persist and refresh query results
Every metric view is automatically a cached materialized result with a fixed grain
Materialized views only define labels and never store results
explanation: Reusable metric definitions and precomputed results solve different concerns. Choose and combine governed semantic definitions and materialized summaries according to the workload.
